div.div:
It takes the Unicode code point (e.g., U+0041 for 'A').
It queries the operating system's font shaping engine (like FreeType on Linux, CoreText on macOS, or DirectWrite on Windows) and requests the vector outline for that character from your active terminal font.

text.tspan: It takes the Unicode code point (e.g., U+0041 for 'A').
It queries the operating system's font shaping engine (like FreeType
on Linux, CoreText on macOS, or DirectWrite on Windows) and
requests the vector outline for that character from your active terminal
font.

div.div: The Optimization (Glyph Atlases): Rendering vector outlines for every single character on every frame would destroy CPU performance. Instead, terminals use a glyph cache. Frequently used characters are rendered once into a texture atlas (a GPU memory sheet), and the terminal treats them as pre-rendered bitmap textures

text.tspan: The Optimization (Glyph Atlases): Rendering vector outlines for every
single character on every frame would destroy CPU performance.
Instead, terminals use a glyph cache. Frequently used characters are
rendered once into a texture atlas (a GPU memory sheet), and the
terminal treats them as pre-rendered bitmap textures
